notes: Chikadze started well at range with kicks, many of them to the body, while Brito kept walking forward behind punches.
The finish came from a scramble: Chikadze slipped throwing a high kick and Brito jumped into top position.
Brito's ground strikes got heavier and turned into repeated hammerfists on a dazed Chikadze until the stoppage.
context: Opened the card (early prelims). Both fighters made weight.

notes: Moura controlled most of the round: she caught a kick, tripped O'Neill and landed elbows and short punches from half guard.
Moura went to north-south and attempted an anaconda choke but lost the grip.
O'Neill came back from the bottom, lifting Moura, rotating her hips and rolling straight into a belly-down armbar for the tap.
Sherdog called it a Submission of the Year contender, and it earned a Performance of the Night bonus.
context: Early prelims. Won from a losing position. Performance of the Night. Both made weight.

notes: A low-kick-led, jab-and-one-two game plan from the center of the cage. Ferreira's output was very low, especially in R1.
Shahbazyan added body kicks in R2. Ferreira landed a few big single shots but missed wild overhands and was warned for an eye poke.
Ferreira pushed harder in R3, but Shahbazyan clinched, landed knees and a takedown, then dropped him with a right hand late.
Sherdog's three scorers had it 30-27 Shahbazyan, sweeping all rounds.
context: Early prelims. A clear decision with no controversy. Both made weight.

notes: The opening feeling-out was short: Gandra landed a low kick, a body jab and a left hook, and Diaz answered with a jab, an elbow and an inside leg kick.
A long punching combination backed Diaz onto the fence while he covered up.
An overhand right dropped Diaz, and Gandra followed up with unanswered punches for the stoppage.
context: Opened the prelims. Gandra's third straight first-round finish (theScore). Both made weight.

notes: R1 was a high-impact striking exchange. Aswell's leg kicks and overhand rights carried the round, and he stopped a takedown with a front headlock and knee.
In R2, Aswell held double underhooks in the clinch and kneed the body, while Yoo landed the cleaner combinations and a left hook. The round split Sherdog's scorers 2-1 for Yoo.
Yoo raised his pace in R3, took Aswell down midway and passed to side control before Aswell scrambled up late.
Sherdog's scorers had it 2-1 for Yoo (29-28), but the official judges went 2-1 for Aswell, making it a close, disputable decision.
context: theScore called Aswell's win an upset (Yoo was the favorite). Split decision that went against two of Sherdog's three scorers. Both made weight.

notes: R1 was a wild brawl. Despaigne dropped Tuivasa early, took him down, got to mount and landed hammerfists, then Tuivasa got his own takedown and punched from the top.
Despaigne was badly fatigued from R2 on. Tuivasa won R2 through clinch work and knees, although Despaigne landed a throw to side control.
R3: Tuivasa dropped Despaigne with a leg kick, but Despaigne landed another throw and punched from half guard for much of the round, with both men exhausted.
Sherdog's scorers had it 2-1 for Tuivasa (29-28). The official judges went 2-1 for Despaigne.
context: Close, disputable split decision. Tuivasa's eighth straight UFC loss, tying the promotion record for a losing streak (theScore). Both made weight.

method_detail: TKO (submission to punch, left hook to the body)
notes: Jourdain used southpaw low kicks and body work, but Vera caught kicks and tripped him to the mat twice in R1 (10-9 Vera on all Sherdog cards).
Vera took over R2: a left uppercut dropped Jourdain, he added another trip with punches on the ground, and a clinch knee scored a second knockdown late.
In R3, a left hook to the body followed by one to the head made Jourdain collapse and wave off the fight.
Vera wore Jourdain down steadily and was ahead on every card before the finish.
context: Bout moved from UFC Fight Night: du Plessis vs. Usman (July). Vera snapped a four-fight losing streak (theScore). Both made weight.

notes: Baraniewski (unbeaten coming in) won R1 clearly: clubbing right hands hurt Menifield several times, then a takedown to full mount and back control.
Baraniewski faded badly from R2 (fatigue, damaged nose). Menifield took over with jabs, power punches and dirty boxing to win the round.
R3 was mostly clinch work on the fence. Baraniewski got an early takedown and landed knees from double underhooks, while Menifield finished stronger with punches, elbows and low kicks.
Sherdog's scorers had it 2-1 for Menifield, matching the official split.
context: Opened the main card. Menifield fought with a visibly damaged thumb from R1. Baraniewski's first pro loss. Both made weight.

notes: Steveson opened with a hard low kick.
Sharaf answered with a clean left hook that knocked Steveson out on his feet, then landed a few hammerfists before the referee stepped in.
No grappling happened. Steveson's wrestling never came into play.
context: Huge upset: Steveson (Olympic wrestling gold medalist, undefeated) was around -2400 per Sherdog, and Sharaf came in 0-2 in the UFC. The bout was moved up to the main card after Ortega vs. Moicano was cancelled days before the event. Third-fastest heavyweight finish in UFC history (theScore). Sharaf received a $100K bonus.

notes: It was a competitive boxing match early. Choi worked jabs to the body and head and landed an overhand right and a left hook.
Freire's body shots, hooks from both hands and kicks opened a cut over Choi's right eye.
Freire froze Choi with an overhand right, pushed him to the mat with follow-up shots and finished with ground punches and elbows.
context: Freire's best UFC win, taking him to 2-2 in the promotion. Both made weight.

notes: Ruffy won the early striking exchanges with low kicks, a body jab and a clean right that stunned Tsarukyan.
Tsarukyan's single-leg attempt failed, and he spent most of the round clinching on the fence and working behind Ruffy without much progress, while looking for elbows.
With seconds left in R1, Tsarukyan closed the distance and knocked Ruffy out with an elbow, landing two more as Ruffy fell.
context: Co-main event. Ruffy replaced Charles Oliveira (announced Aug 5, about 6 weeks out, so not really short notice). Tsarukyan fought through a badly swollen left eye (CBS). Performance of the Night. Both made weight.

notes: Pantoja's wrestling won R1 (body-lock takedown within 10 seconds, mount, elbows) and R4 (long top control in side control and half guard with elbows late). Sherdog gave him both rounds 3-0.
Van's boxing won R2, R3 and R5. His jab, right hands and multi-punch bursts outlanded Pantoja on the feet, and he stuffed several takedowns and even reversed to the top.
Van dropped Pantoja with a one-two in R5 and finished the round on top, clearly the fresher fighter. Sherdog's scorers had it 48-47 Van.
Pantoja complained of head butts in R2 and R3 and was cut over the left eye, but no point was taken.
context: Van's title defense and a rematch of UFC 323 (Dec 2025), which ended in 26 seconds with a Pantoja arm injury. Controversial scorecard: judge Ron McCarthy's 50-45 (giving Van R4) was publicly called 'not possible' by CSAC's Andy Foster, though the result itself isn't in dispute. Fight of the Night. Both made weight at 125.
